newsitem.title: SPAIN: EMU must involve as many states as possible - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: EMU must involve as many states as possible - Arthuis.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in an interview published on Monday that France was eager to include as many European states as possible in monetary union from the start.
"France wants the greatest number of European states as possible in a monetary union from January 1, 1996," he told Spanish daily Cinco Dias.
On Spain, Italy and Portugal's entry, Arthuis said although France shared common ideas with the southern counties, each state was in a different position.
"I don't see any reason why we should consider today that the situation of the three countries will be the same from the beginning," he said.
"The situation of each country is different, each is making important efforts...we will see where we are at the beginning of 1998."
Arthuis will meet Spanish Finance Minister Rodrigo Rato in Madrid later on Monday to discuss European Monetary Union (EMU) and other international issues.
The French minister congratulated Spain's efforts to secure its EMU entry from the start.
"I have full confidence in the determination of the government and the Spanish people," he said.
In the Madrid talks, Arthuis said on Friday he would discuss the follow-up to the European Union's summit in Dublin which laid the groundwork for the practical running of monetary union.

The forthcoming ministerial meeting of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) in Paris in May and the Group of Seven nations meeting in Washington in April will also be topics of discussion.
The talks will end with a news conference at 1200 GMT, the Spanish Finance Ministry said.
